title: PART 2 / SECRET INGREDIENTS
goal: Gather visual clues, read Chapter One, and use evidence to explore character choices behind the friendship conflict.
outcomes: Identify relevant details and make one inference from the clue scene.
Record important events, clues, and character choices from Chapter One.
Explain a character choice or conflict using story evidence.
focus: Look for observations and character inferences supported by evidence, rather than guesses alone.
assessment: Clue Hunt: students name a visible detail and support one quick inference. Small Bite: For either Conflict Report/Zenix Debrief or Character Profile, look for conclusions supported by evidence from Chapter 1.

rows.description: Play the 3-minute scene. Students jot 2–3 visible clues in a notebook or on paper while it plays.

rows.text: Invite 1–2 students to share what they noticed before showing the Clue Tracker. Distinguish observations from guesses.
What might be inside the CONFIDENTIAL envelope, and what clue supports that idea?
Before reading, students jot or sketch one prediction about Chapter One.

rows.description: Read independently, with a partner or group, or as a teacher read-aloud.

rows.text: For either format, students record 2–3 important details: a clue, a character choice, or something that changes their prediction. Short notes or sketches are fine.
Use the Conflict Report and Zenix Debrief prompts from the original lesson slides 17–18. Students discuss in pairs or small groups; a short written response is optional.
What hurt Maddie most about the team switch? What evidence supports that view?

rows.description: One per student choosing Small Bite B

rows.text: Students record 2–3 story facts, one character inference, supporting evidence, and one remaining question.
Which clue or character choice matters most so far, and what supports your thinking?

bonuses.description: — Optional +10–15 min: examine the team discrepancy, false leads, and additional observations.
— Optional +15–20 min: expand the character profile and distinguish evidence from imagination.
